solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Cordial grand coalition’s over for our times (8)

indicatorNotes.over for: O is put in the place of CE: the over stands in for our times

blocks.note: G = grand, a thousand
an alliance is a coalition
CE = Common Era, the dating system of our times; it comes out of ALLIANCE
O = over, the cricket abbreviation; it takes the place of CE

annotation.surface: A political pundit declares the era of grand coalitions finished.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' looks like an adjective describing the coalition; it is a noun, a sweet liqueur. An over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket, abbreviated O.
annotation.definitionFit: Galliano is a sweet yellow Italian liqueur, and a cordial can mean a liqueur.

entries.clue: Florid court poet forgetting line (7)

indicatorNotes.forgetting: the laureate forgets L, so it drops out

blocks.note: the Poet Laureate is the poet attached to the royal court
L = line; removed from the front

annotation.surface: A royal poet writes flowery verse and loses his thread.
annotation.walkthrough: The Poet Laureate is Britain's official royal poet, appointed by the monarch.
annotation.definitionFit: Aureate means golden, and hence of style, elaborately ornate or florid.

entries.clue: Surgical procedure wasted copious lint (11)

indicatorNotes.wasted: wrecked, so the letters are ruined into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: An operation squanders great quantities of surgical dressing.
annotation.walkthrough: Lint is a soft fabric used to dress wounds, which keeps the whole surface in the operating theatre.
annotation.definitionFit: Liposuction is the cosmetic surgical removal of fat by suction.

entries.clue: Stop in state capital of Tennessee (5)

indicatorNotes.capital of: a capital letter is the first one

blocks.note: to aver is to state firmly
first letter of Tennessee

annotation.surface: A traveller makes a stop in Nashville, the state capital of Tennessee.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State capital' reads as one phrase, a city such as Nashville; the words split, with 'state' a verb and 'capital' the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: To avert something is to prevent it, to stop it happening.

entries.clue: Old couple drinking last drops of sloe gin outdoors (4,3)

indicatorNotes.drinking: the pair takes EN inside, as a drinker takes in liquid
indicatorNotes.last drops of: the final letters of each word

blocks.note: O = old
a couple is a pair
last letters of sloE and giN, drunk inside PAIR

annotation.surface: An elderly pair sit outside finishing off the sloe gin.
annotation.walkthrough: Sloe gin is a liqueur made by steeping sloes, the fruit of the blackthorn, in gin.
annotation.definitionFit: Open air means outdoors; the enumeration (4,3) treats it as a phrase.
annotation.definitionNote: 'outdoors' is an adverb and OPEN AIR a noun phrase; both work after 'in the' / as location, e.g. 'drinking outdoors' ~ 'drinking in the open air'.

entries.clue: Raised rent for auditors (6)

indicatorNotes.for auditors: auditors are listeners, so the word is heard, not seen

blocks.note: to rent something is to hire it

annotation.surface: A landlord puts the rent up, and the accountants take note.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Auditors' are accountants in the surface picture; here they are simply hearers, for whom HIRE and HIGHER are the same sound.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a shelf that has been raised now sits higher.

entries.clue: Rush with small team to replace middle management (9)

indicatorNotes.to replace middle: the new letters take the place of the central letter of HURRY

blocks.note: to rush is to hurry; its middle R goes out
S = small
a band is a group or team

annotation.surface: Rushed restructuring brings in a small team to take over from middle managers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Middle management' reads as a tier of staff; 'middle' in fact picks out the central letter of HURRY, and 'management' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Husbandry is careful management of resources, as in good husbandry of funds.

entries.clue: Talk at length and catch up (3)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to bag a fish or a rabbit is to catch it; it is read upwards

annotation.surface: Chat at length and get up to date with the news.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Catch up' looks like a phrasal verb meaning to exchange news, which fits the talking; it is 'catch' plus a reversal signal.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym, as in 'the gift of the gab': idle, lengthy chatter.

entries.clue: Tragedy of poor Lear, etc (7)

indicatorNotes.poor: in a bad state, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A comment on the tragedy of poor King Lear and the like.
annotation.walkthrough: Lear sends the solver to Shakespeare, but the tragedy wanted is Greek: Electra, by Sophocles or Euripides.
annotation.definitionFit: Electra is a Greek tragedy, written by both Sophocles and Euripides.

entries.clue: Sappers gripping boron drills in base (13)

indicatorNotes.drills: boron drills into the word, ending up inside it

blocks.note: RE = Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers
prehensile means able to grip, like a monkey's tail
B is the chemical symbol for boron

annotation.surface: Military engineers hold boron drills at their base camp.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gripping' looks like a verb acting on boron, and 'drills' like a noun; they are an adjective and a verb, with boron boring into PREHENSILE. 'Base' is the definition, in its moral sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Base conduct is low and contemptible, which is reprehensible.

entries.clue: Hound pompous fool engaged in speculative venture (6)

indicatorNotes.engaged in: busy inside, so one goes within the other

blocks.note: a bet is a speculative venture
an ass is a fool, often a pompous one; it goes inside BET

annotation.surface: Someone pesters a self-important idiot who has sunk money into a risky scheme.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hound' looks like a verb, to pester the fool; it is the noun, a dog.
annotation.definitionFit: A basset is a short-legged hunting hound.

entries.clue: Calamitously paralytic, spending penny in haste (8)

indicatorNotes.Calamitously: disastrously, so the letters fall into ruin and a new order
indicatorNotes.spending: a penny spent is gone, so P is removed

blocks.note: the word to be rearranged
P = penny; spent, it leaves PARALYTIC

annotation.surface: A drunk, disastrously incapable, rushes off to the toilet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Paralytic' is British slang for blind drunk, and to 'spend a penny' is a British euphemism for using the toilet, from the old coin-operated public lavatories.
annotation.definitionFit: Alacrity is eager speed, a readiness that shows as haste.

entries.clue: On paper, males aren’t ultimately essential (11)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: at the end, so the last letter

blocks.note: re = on, concerning
a quire is a quantity of paper, 24 or 25 sheets
men are males
last letter of aren't

annotation.surface: A cynical remark that men look necessary only in theory.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On paper' reads as the idiom 'in theory', and 'essential' as an adjective about men; it is a noun, the definition. A quire is an old measure of paper, a small bundle of sheets.
annotation.definitionFit: Used as a noun, an essential is something you cannot do without, as in 'water is a basic requirement'.

entries.clue: In middle of playing recorder, copper appeared again (10)

indicatorNotes.In middle of: CU sits in the middle of the rearranged letters
indicatorNotes.playing: the recorder being played, its letters jumbled

blocks.note: RECORDER rearranged
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper; it goes in the middle

annotation.surface: A policeman turns up again in the middle of a recorder recital.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is British slang for a police officer, which makes the surface a story; here it is the metal.
annotation.definitionFit: To reoccur is to happen or appear again.

entries.clue: United Nations article returning Finland to the Finns without dissent (9)

indicatorNotes.returning: going back, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: UN = United Nations
an is the indefinite article
Suomi is Finland's name for itself; it is reversed

annotation.surface: A UN clause sends Finland back to its own people, and everyone agrees.
annotation.walkthrough: Suomi is the Finnish name for Finland, which 'to the Finns' signals.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a vote carried without dissent had everyone in favour.
annotation.definitionNote: 'without dissent' is a phrase that works as an adjective here: a vote without dissent is a unanimous vote.

entries.clue: Soldiers losing second off-road bike (4)

indicatorNotes.losing: to lose something is to be left without it, so S goes missing from the soldiers

blocks.note: a squad is a small unit of soldiers
S = second; it comes off the front

annotation.surface: Troops lose a moment and an all-terrain vehicle.
annotation.walkthrough: A quad bike is a four-wheeled all-terrain motorbike.
annotation.definitionFit: A quad is short for a quad bike, a four-wheeled off-road vehicle.

entries.clue: Regularly denied vicarship in Romanian city (4)

indicatorNotes.Regularly denied: every other letter is refused, leaving the ones in between

blocks.note: the even letters of vIcArShIp; V, C, R, H and P are denied

annotation.surface: A clergyman is turned down for a parish job in Romania.
annotation.walkthrough: Iasi is a large city in north-east Romania, once the capital of Moldavia.
annotation.definitionFit: Iasi is Romania's second or third largest city.

entries.clue: Attila’s final manoeuvre is uncoordinated (7)

indicatorNotes.final: Attila's final is the one that comes at the end of his name, its last letter

blocks.note: last letter of Attila
a manoeuvre is a planned move to gain an advantage

annotation.surface: A historian judges Attila the Hun's last campaign a shambles.
annotation.walkthrough: Atactic is a rare word, the adjective from ataxia, loss of muscle coordination.
annotation.definitionFit: Atactic means lacking coordination, especially of muscular movement.

entries.clue: Kill snake with axes after husband and I fretted (10)

blocks.note: an asp is a venomous snake
H = husband
the y and x axes of a graph
I as written
to eat can mean to worry or fret, as in 'what's eating you?'

indicatorNotes.after: axes come after husband, so YX is placed second, behind H

annotation.surface: A domestic murder plot involving a snake and an axe, and a nervous husband.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Axes' pictures choppers alongside the snake, but it means graph axes, y and x.
annotation.definitionFit: A method rather than a synonym: to asphyxiate is to kill by cutting off the air supply.

entries.clue: Peru’s First Couple chat with American stars (7)

indicatorNotes.First Couple: a couple is two, and the first couple of a word are its opening two letters

blocks.note: the first two letters of Peru
gas = idle chat
US = American

annotation.surface: Peru's president and spouse chat with Hollywood stars.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First Couple' pictures a president and spouse; it means two letters. 'Stars' looks like celebrities, but it is a constellation.
annotation.definitionFit: Pegasus is a constellation, a group of stars named after the winged horse.
annotation.definitionNote: 'stars' is plural, PEGASUS a single constellation made of stars.

entries.clue: Amateur right back tackling shooter (7)

indicatorNotes.back: sent back the way it came, so right's letters run in reverse
indicatorNotes.tackling: taking hold of, so TR wraps round RIFLE

blocks.note: RT is an abbreviation for right; reversed to TR
a rifle is a gun; it goes inside TR

annotation.surface: A football report: an unpaid right-back brings down the striker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Right back' reads as a football position and 'shooter' as a striker; they are right reversed and a gun.
annotation.definitionFit: A trifler dabbles without seriousness, like an amateur.

entries.clue: Unforgettable ace taking part in The Chase (8)

indicatorNotes.taking part in: A goes inside, becoming part of the chase

blocks.note: hunting is the chase
A = ace, in cards; it sits inside HUNTING

annotation.surface: A star player makes a memorable appearance on the TV quiz The Chase.
annotation.walkthrough: The Chase is a British television quiz show, which makes the ace a star contestant; here 'the chase' is just hunting.
annotation.definitionFit: A haunting melody or image is one you cannot forget.

entries.clue: Abstract, inane ideas on origin of Parks and Recreation (6)

indicatorNotes.inane: empty, so IDEAS loses its insides and leaves I…S
indicatorNotes.origin of: the origin of a word is where it starts, its first letter
indicatorNotes.on: IS is placed after the rest, on it in an across entry

blocks.note: first letter of Parks
rec is short for recreation, as in rec room
IDEAS emptied of its middle

annotation.surface: A summary dismisses the pointless ideas behind the TV sitcom Parks and Recreation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parks and Recreation' reads as the sitcom's title, but it splits into P and REC. 'Abstract' is a noun, a summary, not an adjective describing ideas.
annotation.definitionFit: A precis is a short summary of a text, an abstract.

entries.clue: Food from grandpa’s table (5)

indicatorNotes.from: the answer is taken from within the words

blocks.note: grandPA'S TAble

annotation.surface: A meal served at grandfather's table.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is complete and innocent; the answer runs across the apostrophe.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: pasta is one kind of food, and the broad word covers it.

entries.clue: Careless hoteliers lost cat (13)

indicatorNotes.Careless: sloppily handled, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: Negligent hotel owners have mislaid a guest's cat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lost' belongs to the fodder, not the surface verb it seems to be.
annotation.definitionFit: A tortoiseshell is a cat with mottled black, orange and cream fur.

entries.clue: Hear you can finally flee (3)

indicatorNotes.finally: at the end, so last letters

blocks.note: last letters of heaR, yoU, caN

annotation.surface: An urgent warning that you are free to escape.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hear you' tempts a solver to hunt for a sound-alike U; it is just the first two of three words whose last letters are taken.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in 'run for your life': to get away fast from danger.

entries.clue: Extremely censorious about my cakes (6)

indicatorNotes.Extremely: the extreme letters, first and last
indicatorNotes.about: turned about, so CS becomes SC

blocks.note: outer letters of CensoriouS, turned about
one's = my, as in 'one does one's best'

annotation.surface: Someone is very judgemental about the baking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', but it reverses CS. ONE'S as 'my' is the formal pronoun for oneself.
annotation.definitionFit: Scones are small plain cakes, often served with jam and cream.

entries.clue: Switch on tea-maker for top performer (4,4)

blocks.note: to start a machine is to switch it on
a tea urn boils water for large amounts of tea

annotation.surface: Instructions to put the kettle on for the headline act.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer's own word break is a trap: the wordplay splits one letter later, so looking for STAR and TURN in the clue finds nothing.
annotation.definitionFit: A star turn is the main act, the best performer in a show.
